title: demo-gate
intention: A DEMO gate: a proof executed IN FRONT OF Akien, bound per-node at cast time on the work he wants to watch. Not a stage — a gate. It seals through the quorum door that already exists, with Akien as the reviewer and CC as the notary.
why: The founding reason Cairn was started over, in Akien's words: the prior system 'didn't have the proving structure there. and we didn't have me trying to be insistent on showing me each thing working.' DEMO is that second half made structural instead of remembered. It is also the honest answer to a failure this system has already shown twice in two sessions — a component reported complete because its internal work was complete, while the thing it exists to do was never connected (the quorum gate with nowhere to sign; inference_domain with no host). A green proof did not catch either. A human watching it work would have.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. A demo is that proof with a witness; a hollow build survives a green suite far more easily than it survives being watched.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured, and a demonstration is a measurement taken in the world rather than in the test harness.
telos — the founding intention of getting Akien out of RUNNING the system is not the same as getting him out of SEEING it. DEMO is deliberately his time spent, on the nodes he chooses.

proves_green.prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the proof and emits a VALIDATION.

falsifier.proves_red: A node with DEMO bound cannot reach PROVED without a DEMO validation, and the append door must REFUSE the transition otherwise — not warn, refuse. The validation must carry Akien as the verdict-giver and a DIFFERENT hand as notary; quorum.seal() already refuses a notary who also reviewed, so a self-sealed demo is refused for free and that refusal must be proven, not assumed. A hollow build — a DEMO flag that records a boolean nobody signed, or a node that reaches PROVED with the flag set and no validation — fails.
falsifier.horizon: Re-read after the first three demos. The open question deliberately not answered: what happens when a demo goes RED. It should kick back to build (CP2, the same disposition as a red proof) rather than being a veto, but no demo has been run and guessing the routing ahead of one is inventing physics for a case we have not seen.
